clf-ini-081.text: A cloud architect needs an asynchronous system to process purchase orders. After a customer completes payment, the order data must be placed in a durable queue so backend servers can process each message at their own pace without losing work if a server fails. Which managed AWS service provides this message queue?
clf-ini-081.explanation: Amazon SQS is a fully managed scalable message-queue service that decouples distributed components by storing messages reliably until consumers process them.
clf-ini-081.hint: Look for the AWS service whose acronym includes the word Queue and is designed to decouple components through durable messaging.
optionRationales: Amazon SNS uses a publish/subscribe push model to fan messages out to subscribers; it is not a durable pull-based work queue for individual message processing.
Amazon SQS is a fully managed scalable message-queue service that decouples distributed components by storing messages reliably until consumers process them.
Amazon S3 stores persistent objects such as files and backups and is not a managed work-queue service for short-lived application messages.
Route 53 Traffic Flow manages DNS traffic-routing policies and has no role in application message queues.

clf-ini-082.text: An insurance company uses AWS Auto Scaling to manage its web servers. Management wants to understand the core scaling components. What is the configuration object that defines how new EC2 instances should be launched, including the AMI ID, instance type, networking, and security settings?
clf-ini-082.explanation: A Launch Template defines the EC2 launch parameters that Auto Scaling uses to create new instances, including the AMI, instance type, network configuration, and other settings.
clf-ini-082.hint: Think of the declarative template that acts as the blueprint for launching identical EC2 instances.
optionRationales: A Launch Template defines the EC2 launch parameters that Auto Scaling uses to create new instances, including the AMI, instance type, network configuration, and other settings.
A Target Group belongs to Elastic Load Balancing and groups destinations that receive routed traffic; it is not the EC2 launch blueprint.
Target Tracking is a scaling-policy type that adjusts capacity according to a target metric such as CPU utilization; it does not define the EC2 boot configuration.
A VPC provides networking constructs such as IP ranges and subnets, but it does not replace the EC2 Launch Template used by Auto Scaling.

clf-ini-083.text: A large news portal wants one newly published article event to immediately trigger the same notification to several independent destinations: one system sends SMS, another sends email, and another invokes a Lambda function. Which AWS service provides this publish/subscribe fan-out pattern?
clf-ini-083.explanation: Amazon SNS is a push-based publish/subscribe messaging service that can fan one published message out to multiple subscribers such as email endpoints, SMS recipients, SQS queues, and Lambda functions.
clf-ini-083.hint: Think of the AWS publish/subscribe service designed to push the same notification to multiple subscribed destinations.
optionRationales: Amazon SQS stores messages in queues for consumers to process rather than natively broadcasting one message simultaneously to many independent subscribers.

Amazon SNS is a push-based publish/subscribe messaging service that can fan one published message out to multiple subscribers such as email endpoints, SMS recipients, SQS queues, and Lambda functions.
Amazon EventBridge Scheduler schedules future invocations according to time-based rules and is not the general-purpose SNS fan-out service.
AWS Step Functions orchestrates multi-step workflows and state machines and is more complex than the simple publish/subscribe fan-out requirement described here.

clf-ini-084.text: A company runs Docker containers with Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), but the development team wants a purely serverless container strategy with no need to provision, patch, manage, or select underlying EC2 server fleets. Which compute engine should be selected?
clf-ini-084.explanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers used with Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS. It runs containers without requiring customers to provision or manage the underlying EC2 instances.
clf-ini-084.hint: Consider the serverless container compute option billed according to the CPU and memory resources allocated to running tasks or pods.
optionRationales: AWS Lambda runs short event-driven functions and is not the standard compute engine for long-running ECS container tasks.
AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers used with Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS. It runs containers without requiring customers to provision or manage the underlying EC2 instances.
On-Demand EC2 instances use the traditional IaaS model in which the customer is responsible for the guest operating system and underlying server fleet configuration.
AWS OpsWorks automates server configuration with tools such as Chef or Puppet and is not a serverless container compute engine.

clf-ini-085.text: A solutions architect is designing routing for a microservices web application. Traffic decisions must be made at OSI Layer 7 by inspecting HTTP headers, cookies, methods, and URL paths such as routing '/payments/*' to a specific service. Which Elastic Load Balancing type is designed for this requirement?
clf-ini-085.explanation: An Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and supports advanced HTTP/HTTPS routing based on attributes such as hostnames, URL paths, headers, and request methods.
clf-ini-085.hint: Identify the modern load balancer whose name directly indicates application-layer awareness.
optionRationales: A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and is optimized for very high-throughput TCP/UDP connections rather than inspecting HTTP paths and headers.
An Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and supports advanced HTTP/HTTPS routing based on attributes such as hostnames, URL paths, headers, and request methods.
A Gateway Load Balancer is designed to transparently route network traffic through virtual appliances such as third-party firewalls and security devices.
A Classic Load Balancer is a previous-generation load balancer and lacks many of the advanced Layer 7 routing capabilities available in the ALB.

clf-ini-086.text: A shoe retailer uses Amazon Route 53 for global DNS. The company wants an active-passive routing policy that sends users to a primary endpoint and automatically routes them to a backup endpoint when health checks determine that the primary is unavailable. Which Route 53 routing policy should be used?
clf-ini-086.explanation: Route 53 Failover Routing supports active-passive architectures by routing traffic to a primary resource and switching to a secondary resource when health checks indicate that the primary has failed.
clf-ini-086.hint: Think of the infrastructure term for automatically transferring service to a redundant system after the primary system fails.
optionRationales: Route 53 Failover Routing supports active-passive architectures by routing traffic to a primary resource and switching to a secondary resource when health checks indicate that the primary has failed.
Latency-based routing sends users to the AWS endpoint expected to provide the lowest network latency.
Geolocation routing directs users according to their geographic origin and is useful for location-specific experiences rather than primary/backup failover.
Weighted routing distributes traffic among multiple resources according to configured percentages or weights and is commonly used for gradual rollouts or traffic splitting.

clf-ini-087.text: A software company runs hundreds of large containerized web applications and has standardized on the open-source Kubernetes ecosystem because of team expertise and compatibility with third-party tooling. Which fully managed AWS service reduces the operational effort of provisioning and maintaining the Kubernetes control plane?
clf-ini-087.explanation: Amazon EKS is AWS's managed Kubernetes service and manages the Kubernetes control plane so customers do not have to operate the control-plane infrastructure themselves.
clf-ini-087.hint: Look for the AWS service whose name explicitly includes Kubernetes.
optionRationales: Amazon ECS is AWS's native container-orchestration service and uses AWS-specific APIs and control models rather than a Kubernetes control plane.
Amazon EKS is AWS's managed Kubernetes service and manages the Kubernetes control plane so customers do not have to operate the control-plane infrastructure themselves.
Elastic Beanstalk automates deployment of application environments but is not a managed Kubernetes control-plane service.
EC2 Instance Store provides ephemeral local block storage attached to compute hosts and is unrelated to container orchestration.

clf-ini-088.text: An infrastructure analyst wants to understand Amazon SQS message behavior. After a backend consumer successfully receives a message from a queue and begins processing it, what happens automatically to the message from the perspective of other consumers?
options: The message is permanently deleted from AWS immediately when the receive call begins.
The message becomes temporarily invisible to other consumers for a configurable period called the Visibility Timeout.
The message is irreversibly encrypted by AWS Artifact keys.
The message is automatically emailed to every root-account administrator.
clf-ini-088.explanation: Receiving a message from Amazon SQS does not automatically delete it. SQS hides the message from other consumers for the Visibility Timeout so one worker can process it, and the consumer should explicitly delete it after successful processing.
clf-ini-088.hint: Consider the timed mechanism that temporarily hides a task from other workers while the current consumer processes it.
optionRationales: Receiving a message from Amazon SQS does not automatically delete it. SQS hides the message from other consumers for the Visibility Timeout so one worker can process it, and the consumer should explicitly delete it after successful processing.
If SQS deleted a message as soon as it was received, the task could be lost if the worker failed before finishing processing.
SQS is a managed messaging service for application components and does not provide a built-in feature that emails every queue message to human administrators.
AWS Artifact stores compliance reports and agreements and does not interact with application-message streams.

clf-ini-089.text: A solutions architect needs a load balancer for a critical financial application that must handle millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency at the raw connection level using OSI Layer 4 networking. Which Elastic Load Balancing type is best suited to this high-throughput profile?
clf-ini-089.explanation: A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and is designed for very high-throughput TCP, UDP, and TLS connection handling with extremely low latency.
clf-ini-089.hint: Look for the load balancer whose name and purpose focus on raw network-level connections.
optionRationales: An Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and inspects HTTP application data, which is not the raw high-throughput Layer 4 model described here.
A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and is designed for very high-throughput TCP, UDP, and TLS connection handling with extremely low latency.
A Gateway Load Balancer is used to transparently route network traffic through virtual appliances such as security firewalls and inspection systems.
A Classic Load Balancer is a previous-generation option and is generally not chosen for new architectures requiring the NLB's extreme Layer 4 performance characteristics.

clf-ini-090.text: A department-store chain places Amazon CloudFront in front of its AWS application to accelerate product images and dynamic web content for users on multiple continents. What is the official name for the globally distributed edge points of presence that CloudFront uses to cache and deliver content close to end users?
clf-ini-090.explanation: Edge Locations are AWS points of presence used by services such as Amazon CloudFront to cache and deliver content closer to users around the world.
clf-ini-090.hint: Think of the AWS global-infrastructure term for facilities positioned at the network edge to deliver cached content close to users.
optionRationales: Availability Zones are isolated locations within Regions used to host primary AWS resources such as EC2 and RDS; they are not CloudFront edge-cache points of presence.
Edge Locations are AWS points of presence used by services such as Amazon CloudFront to cache and deliver content closer to users around the world.
Local Zones extend selected compute and storage services closer to specific metropolitan areas but are not the global CDN edge-location network.
AWS Regions are large geographic areas containing multiple Availability Zones and are not the edge points of presence used for CDN caching.
